examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Linear Combination of Two Matrices
examples.worked_solution:
We multiply each entry of $A$ by $2$ and each entry of $B$ by $\dfrac{1}{2},$ and then add the resulting matrices, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2A+\frac{1}{2}B & =2[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 5 \\ 2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0 & \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot 4 & \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2+0 & 10+1 \\ 2+2 & 4+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 11 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
If $kA=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -21 & 56\end{aligned}]$,
where $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 8\end{aligned}]$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To express $kA,$ we multiply each entry of $A$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kA & =k\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-k & -3k & 8k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kA$ in the problem statement:

$$
[\begin{aligned}-k & -3k & 8k\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -21 & 56\end{aligned}]
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the leftmost elements, $-k$ and $-7.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-k & =-7 \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.
